explicit direction of 2026-08-16: "one more round then manual verify and close."

WHAT VERIFIED, AND ON WHAT SURFACE. Six cross-provider verification rounds ran
through the sanctioned Step 6 command (python -m ai_router.verify_session),
every one against verifier model gpt-5-6-sol, effective provider OPENAI, with
the orchestrator's own provider (anthropic, via model-registry lookup on

session-verification task type. Raw artifacts, all committed in the session-set
directory: s5-verification.md and s5-verification-fanout-2.md (round 1,
two-lens discovery), s5-verification-round-2.md (supplementary),
s5-verification-round-3.md, -round-4.md, -round-5.md, -round-6.md, with
structured findings in s5-issues.json and s5-issues-round-{2,3,4,5,6}.json and
the round ledger in s5-rounds.jsonl. Timestamps run 2026-08-16T06:44 through
2026-08-16T09:2x local. Total routed verification cost for the session:
approximately $4.05 across the six rounds.

WHY THIS IS AN ATTESTED CLOSE RATHER THAN A VERIFIED ONE. Rounds 4, 5 and 6 each
ran on a recorded --operator-authorized-round attestation past the bounded two
remediation-review cycles. Round 6 accepted seven of eight fix verdicts and
rejected one, and its finding was remediated afterwards -- so the final state of
the tree is FIXED AND UNREVIEWED. The authorized rounds are spent, and this
session does not self-authorize another; the operator directed the close to
proceed on this path regardless of the outcome.

WHAT THE LAST FINDING WAS AND WHAT WAS DONE. Round 6 rejected criterion I5's
post-capture evidence as self-certifying: the degraded path wrote
postCaptureStep: "ran" into its manifest and the parent read that same field
back out as proof. Nothing had executed. It is fixed by making the step perform
real work -- it now renders the run's step list to a standalone walkthrough
document on the degraded path, which is exactly what the guarantee "failure to
record must never fail the walkthrough" is about -- and the parent derives the
fact from that FILE (marker comment, list items, size floor) rather than from
anything the child asserted. Measured across the three declared variants while
the dependency was genuinely broken: 454, 581 and 448 bytes. Strictly better
than what was rejected; not independently confirmed. Recorded as an owed
residual with a named owner (the operator) in disposition.json, because an
adjudication at the bound settles the STOP, not the truth.

WHAT THE SESSION ESTABLISHED. The container hides the host: a magenta window
raised and held FOREGROUND on the operator's real desktop contributed 0.000000
of every frame captured inside the container, with the magenta detector proved
to fire first at 0.999746 through the identical pipeline, and zero bind mounts
used anywhere. Machine verdict PASS on six scored criteria (I1-I6) plus I7 on
presence, three clean runs and one run interrupted while capture was OBSERVED
producing bytes, scored by a separate script that reads the criteria file and
refuses to score a measurement whose stamped digest no longer matches it. The
cheap mitigation was measured first and does NOT dominate: OBS's
--only-bundled-plugins removes one module of twenty-five and leaves 317 MB of
bundled surface including an embedded Chromium and the camera path.

SUITES, ALL RE-RUN AFTER THE LAST CODE CHANGE AND ALL FRESH: pytest 4986 passed
/ 5 skipped / 1 xfailed (293.6s, -n 8 per the operator's standing parallelism
cap), mocha 1548 passing (19s), Layer 3 Playwright 37 passed (3.4m).

WHAT THIS CLOSE DOES NOT CLAIM. The Dabbler extension is INSTALLED and VS Code
runs with it; activation and Work Explorer rendering under Linux software
rendering are unobserved. OBS runs in the container and did not produce a clean
capture of the target, because its own window stays mapped on the display it
records. Layer 3 reuse remains partial and round 6 marked it
accepted-with-modification rather than resolved. Nothing here says anything
about Windows display scaling, tutorial-length recordings, or a first-build cost
on a clean machine. All of it is in disposition.residuals.
